original_english: Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and are mostly dead.
hinglish_roman: Sclerenchyma cells mein thin walls hoti hain aur yeh living cells hote hain.
hinglish_with_error: Sclerenchyma cells mein thin walls hoti hain aur yeh living cells hote hain.
error_word: thin walls hoti hain aur yeh living cells hote hain
correct_word: thick lignified walls hoti hain aur yeh mostly dead cells hote hain
explanation: Student ne sclerenchyma ki properties galat likhi hain. 'Thin walls' aur 'living' dono galat hain. Sclerenchyma ki walls thick aur lignified hoti hain aur yeh cells mostly dead hote hain. Yeh collenchyma ki properties se confuse ho sakti hain.

original_english: Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.
hinglish_roman: Xylem leaves se food ko roots tak transport karta hain.
hinglish_with_error: Xylem leaves se food ko roots tak transport karta hain.
explanation: 'Xylem' ek singular subject hai isliye 'karta hai' hona chahiye, 'karta hain' nahi. 'Hain' plural subjects ke saath use hota hai. Iske alawa yeh sentence factually bhi galat hai kyunki xylem food nahi balki water aur minerals transport karta hai - woh phloem ka kaam hai.

original_english: Tendons connect muscles to bones.
hinglish_roman: Tendons bones ko bones se connecting hain.
hinglish_with_error: Tendons bones ko bones se connecting hain.
explanation: Hinglish mein English present participle 'connecting' directly use karna galat hai. Sahi form hai 'connect karte hain' jisme English verb ke saath Hindi auxiliary 'karte hain' lagate hain. Yeh ek common intra-sentential mixing error hai.

original_english: Epithelial tissue forms the outer covering of the body.
hinglish_roman: Epithelial tissue body ke outer covering banata hai.
hinglish_with_error: Epithelial tissue body ke outer covering banata hai.
explanation: Hindi mein 'covering' feminine noun hai isliye 'ki' use hona chahiye, 'ke' nahi. 'Ke' masculine nouns ke saath use hota hai. Yeh ek common gender agreement mistake hai jo Hindi-English mixing mein frequently hoti hai.

original_english: Each neuron has three main parts: cell body, dendrites and axon.
hinglish_roman: Har neuron ke teen main parts hote hain: cell body, dendrites aur axons.
hinglish_with_error: Har neuron ke teen main parts hote hain: cell body, dendrites aur axons.
explanation: Ek neuron mein sirf ek axon hota hai, isliye 'axon' singular use hona chahiye. 'Axons' likh ke student ne galat pluralization ki hai. 'Dendrites' zaroor plural hai kyunki ek neuron mein multiple dendrites hote hain, lekin axon hamesha ek hi hota hai.

original_english: Reproduction is a biological process by which living beings produce new individuals of their own kind.
hinglish_roman: Reproduction ek biological process hai jiske zariye living beings apni hi tarah ke naye individuals paida karte hain.

original_english: Every organism has a definite life span - it is born, grows, matures, reproduces and eventually dies.
hinglish_roman: Har organism ki ek definite life span hoti hai - woh janam leta hai, badhta hai, mature hota hai, reproduce karta hai aur aakhir mein mar jaata hai.

original_english: Living beings reproduce in two main ways - asexually, where a single parent produces offspring that are almost exact copies of the parent, and sexually, where offspring inherit a mix of characteristics from the two individuals.
hinglish_roman: Living beings do tareekon se reproduce karte hain - asexually, jahan ek single parent aisa offspring produce karta hai jo almost parent ki exact copy hota hai, aur sexually, jahan offspring ko dono individuals ki mixed characteristics milti hain.

original_english: Asexual mode of reproduction is seen in many unicellular organisms like bacteria, amoeba, yeast and simple multicellular organisms like hydra and sponge.
hinglish_roman: Asexual reproduction bahut saare unicellular organisms mein dekha jaata hai jaise bacteria, amoeba, yeast aur simple multicellular organisms jaise hydra aur sponge mein.

original_english: Vegetative propagation means that new plants arise from the vegetative parts, that is, from the growing parts of a plant.
hinglish_roman: Vegetative propagation ka matlab hai ki naye plants, plant ke vegetative parts yaani growing parts se nikalte hain.

original_english: Potato and ginger have fleshy underground stems that sprout new plants without producing seeds.
hinglish_roman: Aalu aur adrak ke fleshy underground stems hote hain jo bina seeds produce kiye naye plants uga dete hain.

original_english: Bryophyllum leaves sprout tiny plantlets which eventually grow into new plants.
hinglish_roman: Bryophyllum ke patte chote-chote plantlets ugaate hain jo aakhirkar naye plants ban jaate hain.

original_english: Grafting involves inserting a stem cutting of one plant into a slit made on the rooted plant of another variety.
hinglish_roman: Grafting mein ek plant ki stem cutting ko doosri variety ke rooted plant ke slit mein fit kiya jaata hai.

original_english: In layering, a flexible twig is buried under the soil and after roots develop, it is cut from the parent plant to grow independently.
hinglish_roman: Layering mein ek flexible twig ko mitti ke neeche dabaaya jaata hai aur roots develop hone ke baad, use parent plant se kaat diya jaata hai taaki woh alag grow kar sake.

original_english: Tissue culture technique has revolutionised farming practices like banana farming by providing mass-produced healthy plantlets.
hinglish_roman: Tissue culture technique ne banana farming jaisi farming practices mein revolution la diya hai kyunki isme mass-produced healthy plantlets milte hain.

original_english: In organisms like hydra, repeated cell division at a specific site on the parent body produces a small outgrowth called a bud.
hinglish_roman: Hydra jaise organisms mein, parent body ke ek specific jagah par baar baar cell division hone se ek chhoti si outgrowth banti hai jise bud kehte hain.

original_english: The bud enlarges and separates from the parent to live independently - this process is called budding.
hinglish_roman: Bud bada hota hai aur parent se alag hokar independently jeena shuru karta hai - is process ko budding kehte hain.

original_english: Spores are lightweight, usually single-celled structures that float easily through air currents and germinate quickly into a new individual when moisture and nutrients are available.
hinglish_roman: Spores halke aur aksar single-celled hote hain jo aasaani se hawa ke saath ud jaate hain aur jab naami aur nutrients milein toh jaldi se naye individual mein germinate ho jaate hain.

original_english: In asexual reproduction, the central process is mitosis, a type of cell division that produces two daughter cells each having the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
hinglish_roman: Asexual reproduction mein central process mitosis hai, yeh ek aisa cell division hai jisme do daughter cells banti hain jinmein parent cell jitne hi chromosomes hote hain.

original_english: Offspring produced by asexual reproduction are genetically identical to the parent and are called clones.
hinglish_roman: Asexual reproduction se paida hone waale offspring parent ke genetically identical hote hain aur inhe clones kaha jaata hai.

original_english: Sexual reproduction involves two parents in the formation of a new individual, meaning both parents contribute to the genetic material of the offspring.
hinglish_roman: Sexual reproduction mein do parents milkar ek naya individual banate hain, yaani dono parents offspring ke genetic material mein contribute karte hain.

original_english: Meiosis is a special type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number of a parent cell from diploid to haploid in daughter cells.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis ek special type ka cell division hai jisme parent cell ke chromosomes ki sankhya diploid se haploid ho jaati hai daughter cells mein.

original_english: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, which means a total of 46 chromosomes in each body cell.
hinglish_roman: Insaanon mein 23 pairs of chromosomes hote hain, matlab har body cell mein kul 46 chromosomes hote hain.

original_english: In plants, the pollen grain contains male gametes and delivers them to an ovule which contains the female gamete or egg.
hinglish_roman: Plants mein, pollen grain mein male gametes hote hain jo inhe ovule tak pohonchate hain jahan female gamete yaani egg hota hai.

original_english: Flowers serve as reproductive organs in angiosperms, which are the most diverse group of plants on Earth.
hinglish_roman: Angiosperms mein flowers reproductive organs ki tarah kaam karte hain, aur angiosperms dharti par plants ka sabse diverse group hai.

original_english: A complete flower has four parts - sepals, petals, stamens and pistil.
hinglish_roman: Ek complete flower mein chaar parts hote hain - sepals, petals, stamens aur pistil.

original_english: The stamen is the male part of a flower and consists of a filament and an anther which produces pollen grains containing male gametes.
hinglish_roman: Stamen phool ka male part hota hai aur isme ek filament aur ek anther hota hai jo male gametes wale pollen grains produce karta hai.

original_english: The pistil is the female part of the flower and has three subparts - stigma, style and ovary.
hinglish_roman: Pistil phool ka female part hota hai aur iske teen subparts hote hain - stigma, style aur ovary.

original_english: The stigma is located at the tip of the pistil and may be flat and/or sticky to receive pollen.
hinglish_roman: Stigma pistil ki tip par hota hai aur yeh flat aur/ya sticky ho sakta hai taaki pollen ko pakad sake.

original_english: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower is called pollination.
hinglish_roman: Anther se pollen grains ka stigma tak transfer hona pollination kehlata hai.

original_english: Self-pollination is when pollen transfers to the stigma of the same flower or another flower of the same plant.
hinglish_roman: Self-pollination tab hoti hai jab pollen usi phool ke ya usi plant ke doosre phool ke stigma par transfer hota hai.

original_english: Cross-pollination happens when pollen is transferred from a flower of one plant to the stigma of a flower of another plant of the same type.
hinglish_roman: Cross-pollination tab hoti hai jab pollen ek plant ke phool se doosre same type ke plant ke phool ke stigma par jaata hai.

original_english: Pollination by wind is seen in plants like wheat, maize and rice, where pollen grains are light and small and produced in large numbers.
hinglish_roman: Wheat, maize aur rice jaise plants mein wind se pollination hoti hai, jahan pollen grains halke aur chote hote hain aur badi matra mein produce hote hain.

original_english: Insect-pollinated flowers like sunflower and hibiscus are often brightly coloured, produce nectar and give off fragrance to attract pollinators.
hinglish_roman: Sunflower aur hibiscus jaise insect-pollinated flowers aksar chamkeelay rang ke hote hain, nectar produce karte hain aur pollinators ko attract karne ke liye khushbu dete hain.

original_english: Once pollen reaches a compatible stigma, pollen grains produce pollen tubes that grow down through the style into the ovary.
hinglish_roman: Jab pollen compatible stigma tak pahunch jaata hai, pollen grains pollen tubes banate hain jo style ke zariye ovary mein neeche ki taraf badhti hain.

original_english: The male gamete moves through the pollen tube and arrives at the ovule where it fuses with the egg cell - this fusion is called fertilisation.
hinglish_roman: Male gamete pollen tube se hokar ovule tak pahunchta hai jahan woh egg cell se fuse hota hai - is fusion ko fertilisation kehte hain.

original_english: The fertilised egg is called a zygote, which later develops into an embryo, while the ovary develops into a fruit and ovules develop into seeds.
hinglish_roman: Fertilised egg ko zygote kehte hain jo baad mein embryo ban jaata hai, jabki ovary fruit ban jaati hai aur ovules seeds ban jaate hain.

original_english: Seed dispersal takes place by wind, water or animals, and when conditions like water, air and temperature are favourable, the seed germinates and grows into a new plant.
hinglish_roman: Seeds ka dispersal hawa, paani ya jaanwaron ke zariye hota hai, aur jab paani, hawa aur temperature jaisi conditions suitable hon, toh seed germinate hokar naya plant ban jaata hai.

original_english: In many aquatic animals like frogs and most fish, fertilisation occurs outside the body and is called external fertilisation.
hinglish_roman: Bahut saare aquatic animals jaise mendak aur zyada tar machhliyon mein fertilisation body ke bahar hoti hai aur ise external fertilisation kehte hain.

original_english: In reptiles, birds and mammals, fertilisation takes place inside the body of the female and is called internal fertilisation.
hinglish_roman: Reptiles, birds aur mammals mein fertilisation female ke body ke andar hoti hai aur ise internal fertilisation kehte hain.

original_english: Fish and amphibians produce several hundred to several thousand eggs at a time with yolk, which contains nutritive substances to nourish the developing embryos.
hinglish_roman: Machhliyan aur amphibians ek baar mein kai sau se kai hazaar andey deti hain jinmein yolk hota hai jo develop ho rahe embryos ko poshan deta hai.

original_english: A larva is an intermediate feeding stage in the life cycle of some organisms like butterflies and frogs.
hinglish_roman: Larva titliyon aur mendakon jaise organisms ke life cycle mein ek intermediate feeding stage hota hai.

original_english: The male reproductive system has organs that produce sperm and help them transfer to the female body.
hinglish_roman: Male reproductive system mein aise organs hote hain jo sperm produce karte hain aur unhe female body tak pahunchane mein madad karte hain.

original_english: Sperm are produced in two oval-shaped organs called testes, present in a pouch of skin called the scrotum.
hinglish_roman: Sperm do oval-shaped organs mein bante hain jise testes kehte hain, yeh scrotum naam ki ek skin ki theli mein hote hain.

original_english: The scrotum keeps the testes slightly cooler than normal body temperature, which is necessary for sperm formation.
hinglish_roman: Scrotum testes ko normal body temperature se thoda thanda rakhta hai jo sperm banane ke liye zaroori hai.

original_english: Glands like the seminal vesicles and the prostate add fluids to nourish the sperm and help them remain active and move.
hinglish_roman: Seminal vesicles aur prostate jaise glands sperm ko nourish karne wale fluids add karte hain aur unhe active aur motile rehne mein madad karte hain.

original_english: Each sperm has a head containing genetic material and a long tail that helps it swim towards the egg.
hinglish_roman: Har sperm mein ek head hota hai jisme genetic material hota hai aur ek lamba tail hota hai jo use egg ki taraf swim karne mein madad karta hai.

original_english: The female reproductive system has a pair of ovaries, oviducts or fallopian tubes, a uterus and a vagina.
hinglish_roman: Female reproductive system mein ek pair of ovaries, oviducts yaani fallopian tubes, ek uterus aur ek vagina hota hai.

original_english: The uterus is a bag-like structure where a foetus develops, and it opens into the vagina through a narrow passage called the cervix.
hinglish_roman: Uterus ek theli jaisi structure hoti hai jahan foetus develop hota hai, aur yeh cervix naam ki ek tangi passage ke zariye vagina mein khulta hai.

original_english: The process of the formation of gametes is called gametogenesis and it takes place in the testes and the ovaries.
hinglish_roman: Gametes ke banne ki process ko gametogenesis kehte hain aur yeh testes aur ovaries mein hoti hai.

original_english: In humans, cells have 46 chromosomes but sperm and eggs have only 23 so that when they combine, the zygote has the same number as the parents.
hinglish_roman: Insaanon mein normal cells mein 46 chromosomes hote hain lekin sperm aur eggs mein sirf 23 hote hain taaki jab woh milein toh zygote mein parents jitne chromosomes ho jaayein.

original_english: From puberty onwards, usually one mature egg is released every month from one of the ovaries - this is called ovulation.
hinglish_roman: Puberty ke baad se, aam taur par har mahine ek ovary se ek mature egg release hota hai - ise ovulation kehte hain.

original_english: If a sperm encounters an egg and fuses with it, a zygote is formed and the inner lining of the uterus becomes thicker and richer in blood vessels.
hinglish_roman: Agar sperm egg se milta hai aur usse fuse ho jaata hai toh zygote ban jaata hai aur uterus ki inner lining zyada moti aur blood vessels se bhari ho jaati hai.

original_english: If an egg is not fertilised, it degenerates and the inner lining of the uterus sheds - this process is called menstruation or a period.
hinglish_roman: Agar egg fertilise nahi hota, toh woh khatam ho jaata hai aur uterus ki inner lining girne lagti hai - is process ko menstruation ya period kehte hain.

original_english: The menstrual cycle repeats typically every 21 to 35 days and usually begins at puberty, between the ages of 10 to 14 in girls, and continues until menopause around age 50.
hinglish_roman: Menstrual cycle aam taur par har 21 se 35 din mein repeat hota hai aur puberty ke waqt shuru hota hai jo ladkiyon mein usually 10 se 14 saal ki umar mein hoti hai, aur lagbhag 50 saal ki umar mein menopause tak chalta hai.

original_english: Pregnancy in humans lasts about nine months and is divided into three stages called trimesters.
hinglish_roman: Insaanon mein pregnancy lagbhag nau mahine tak chalti hai aur ise teen stages mein baanta jaata hai jinhe trimesters kehte hain.

original_english: In the first trimester, the fertilised egg develops into an embryo during the first two months and major organs start forming.
hinglish_roman: Pehle trimester mein, pehle do mahino mein fertilised egg embryo ban jaata hai aur major organs banne shuru ho jaate hain.

original_english: From about the ninth week, the developing embryo is called a foetus, which continues to grow and develop through the second and third trimesters.
hinglish_roman: Lagbhag nauwein hafte se, develop ho rahe embryo ko foetus kaha jaata hai jo doosre aur teesre trimester mein barhna aur develop hona jaari rakhta hai.

original_english: During childbirth, strong contractions of the muscles of the uterus help push the foetus out through the birth canal.
hinglish_roman: Prasav ke waqt uterus ki muscles ki tej contractions foetus ko birth canal se bahar dhakelte hain.

original_english: Breastfeeding is essential because a mother's milk provides complete nutrition and protects the infant from many diseases.
hinglish_roman: Breastfeeding bahut zaroori hai kyunki maa ka doodh poori nutrition deta hai aur bacche ko kai bimariyon se bachata hai.

original_english: Sexually Transmitted Infections or STIs include gonorrhoea, herpes, syphilis, genital warts and HIV, which can eventually lead to AIDS.
hinglish_roman: Sexually Transmitted Infections yaani STIs mein gonorrhoea, herpes, syphilis, genital warts aur HIV shamil hain jo aakhirkar AIDS ka kaaran ban sakta hai.

original_english: Using condoms can prevent the transmission of STIs and also help prevent pregnancy.
hinglish_roman: Condom use karne se STIs ka transmission roka ja sakta hai aur yeh pregnancy rokne mein bhi madad karta hai.

original_english: Oral contraceptive pills change the release of eggs by altering hormones, though these may have some side effects.
hinglish_roman: Oral contraceptive pills hormones ko alter karke egg ka release badal deti hain, lekin inke kuch side effects bhi ho sakte hain.

original_english: Intra-Uterine Devices such as Copper-T are placed in the uterus to avoid pregnancy.
hinglish_roman: Copper-T jaise Intra-Uterine Devices ko uterus ke andar rakha jaata hai taaki pregnancy na ho.

original_english: Surgical methods to prevent pregnancy include blocking the vas deferens in males or the fallopian tubes in females.
hinglish_roman: Pregnancy rokne ke surgical methods mein males mein vas deferens aur females mein fallopian tubes ko band karna shamil hai.

original_english: Prenatal sex determination is strictly prohibited by law in India to maintain sex ratio for a healthy society.
hinglish_roman: Prasav se pehle ling nirdharan karna India mein kanoon dwara sakht roop se mana hai taaki samaj mein ling anupaat theek rahe.

original_english: Variation helps some individuals adapt better to changing environments and over time, this process contributes to evolution.
hinglish_roman: Variation kuch individuals ko badlte environments mein behtar adapt karne mein madad karta hai aur yeh process samay ke saath evolution mein contribute karta hai.

original_english: Louis Pasteur proved that new life always comes from pre-existing life and established the germ theory of disease.
hinglish_roman: Louis Pasteur ne prove kiya ki nayi zindagi hamesha pehle se maujood zindagi se aati hai aur unhone germ theory of disease establish ki.

original_english: P. Maheshwari was known as the Father of Indian Embryology and developed the technique of in-vitro fertilisation in flowering plants.
hinglish_roman: P. Maheshwari ko Father of Indian Embryology ke naam se jaana jaata tha aur unhone flowering plants mein in-vitro fertilisation ki technique develop ki.

original_english: In-vitro Fertilisation or IVF is a medical technique in which an egg and a sperm are combined outside the female body in a laboratory dish.
hinglish_roman: In-vitro Fertilisation yaani IVF ek medical technique hai jisme egg aur sperm ko female body ke bahar ek laboratory dish mein combine kiya jaata hai.

original_english: Females have XX sex chromosomes while males have XY chromosomes; the father determines the biological sex of the baby.
hinglish_roman: Females mein XX sex chromosomes hote hain jabki males mein XY hote hain; bacha ka biological sex baap determine karta hai.

original_english: More than 10 lakh ASHA workers are trained community health workers who promote hygiene, immunisation and family planning across India.
hinglish_roman: 10 lakh se zyada ASHA workers trained community health workers hain jo poore India mein hygiene, immunisation aur family planning ko promote karti hain.

original_english: Selective breeding involves farmers choosing plants with desirable characters for reproduction to develop improved crop varieties.
hinglish_roman: Selective breeding mein kisan aise plants ko reproduce karne ke liye choose karte hain jinmein desirable characters hote hain taaki improved crop varieties tayaar ho sakein.

original_english: Asexual reproduction is fast and helps organisms increase their population quickly, especially when environmental conditions are favourable.
hinglish_roman: Asexual reproduction tezi se hoti hai aur organisms ko apni population jaldi badhane mein madad karta hai, khaaskar jab environmental conditions theek hon.

original_english: Fungi grow very fast by spore formation and degrade organic wastes, pollutants and even heavy metals from industrial waste.
hinglish_roman: Fungi spore formation ke zariye bahut tezi se badhte hain aur organic wastes, pollutants aur yahan tak ki industrial waste ke heavy metals ko bhi degrade kar dete hain.

original_english: Penicillin and amoxicillin are antibiotics derived from fungi that have saved countless lives from bacterial infections.
hinglish_roman: Penicillin aur amoxicillin fungi se milne wale antibiotics hain jo bacterial infections se anginat logon ki jaan bacha chuke hain.

original_english: A woman's health during pregnancy plays a vital role in the baby's growth, so she should eat a balanced diet rich in proteins, vitamins and minerals.
hinglish_roman: Pregnancy mein aurat ki sehat bacha ke vikas mein ek important role nibhati hai, isliye use proteins, vitamins aur minerals se bharpur balanced diet lena chahiye.

original_english: Post-partum depression is a recognised condition of anxiety and fatigue experienced by some mothers after delivery.
hinglish_roman: Post-partum depression ek recognised condition hai jisme kuch maaon ko delivery ke baad anxiety aur thakan ka anubhav hota hai.

original_english: Sexual maturity means the body becomes capable of reproduction, but emotional maturity, which takes longer, means handling feelings and making thoughtful decisions.
hinglish_roman: Sexual maturity ka matlab hai ki body reproduce karne mein capable ho jaati hai, lekin emotional maturity, jo zyada waqt leta hai, ka matlab hai feelings ko sambhalna aur sochsamajh ke faisle karna.

original_english: The process of implantation marks the beginning of pregnancy when the zygote embeds itself into the inner lining of the uterus.
hinglish_roman: Implantation ka process pregnancy ki shuruaat ko darshata hai jab zygote apne aap ko uterus ki inner lining mein embed kar leta hai.

original_english: What is the difference between asexual and sexual reproduction?
hinglish_roman: Asexual aur sexual reproduction mein kya difference hota hai?

original_english: Can you explain what vegetative propagation is with examples?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap vegetative propagation ko examples ke saath explain kar sakte ho?

original_english: What exactly is meiosis and why is it important for sexual reproduction?
hinglish_roman: Meiosis exactly kya hoti hai aur sexual reproduction ke liye yeh kyun zaroori hai?

original_english: Give me an example of cross-pollination in everyday plants we see around us.
hinglish_roman: Hamare aas paas ke plants mein cross-pollination ka ek example do.

original_english: What is the definition of fertilisation in plants?
hinglish_roman: Plants mein fertilisation ki definition kya hai?

original_english: How is external fertilisation different from internal fertilisation in animals?
hinglish_roman: Animals mein external fertilisation aur internal fertilisation mein kya fark hai?

original_english: Can you explain the menstrual cycle step by step?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap menstrual cycle ko step by step explain kar sakte ho?

original_english: What are the different contraceptive methods mentioned in the chapter?
hinglish_roman: Chapter mein kaun kaun se contraceptive methods bataye gaye hain?

original_english: Why do plants need pollinators and what happens if pollinators disappear?
hinglish_roman: Plants ko pollinators ki zaroorat kyun hoti hai aur agar pollinators khatam ho jaayein toh kya hoga?

original_english: What is the formula or formula-like rule for calculating the number of chromosome combinations possible during meiosis?
hinglish_roman: Meiosis ke dauran kitne chromosome combinations possible hote hain, iska formula ya rule kya hai?

original_english: Can you give an example of budding in a simple organism?
hinglish_roman: Kisi simple organism mein budding ka ek example de sakte ho?

original_english: What is ovulation and on which day of the menstrual cycle does it usually occur?
hinglish_roman: Ovulation kya hoti hai aur yeh menstrual cycle ke kis din hoti hai usually?

original_english: How do grafting and layering differ as methods of vegetative propagation?
hinglish_roman: Vegetative propagation ke methods mein grafting aur layering mein kya farq hai?

original_english: What is the definition of a zygote and how is it formed?
hinglish_roman: Zygote ki definition kya hai aur yeh kaise banta hai?

original_english: Can you explain with an example why sexual reproduction leads to more variation than asexual reproduction?
hinglish_roman: Kya tum example ke saath explain kar sakte ho ki sexual reproduction mein asexual reproduction se zyada variation kyun hoti hai?

original_english: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma.
hinglish_roman: Pollination anther se pollen ka stigma mein transfer hone ka process hain.
hinglish_with_error: Pollination anther se pollen ka stigma mein transfer hone ka process hain.
error_explanation: 'Process' is singular so the verb should be 'hai' not 'hain'. 'Hain' is used for plural subjects.

original_english: The ovary of a flower develops into a fruit after fertilisation.
hinglish_roman: Fertilisation ke baad phool ki ovary fruit mein badal hoti hai.
hinglish_with_error: Fertilisation ke baad phool ki ovary fruit mein badal hoti hai.
error_explanation: The phrase 'badal hoti hai' is grammatically incomplete; the correct form is 'badal jaati hai' which indicates a change/transformation using the completive auxiliary 'jaana'.

original_english: Sperm are produced in the testes and travel through the vas deferens.
hinglish_roman: Sperm testes mein banta hain aur vas deferens se travel karta hain.
hinglish_with_error: Sperm testes mein banta hain aur vas deferens se travel karta hain.
error_explanation: 'Sperm' here is treated as plural (millions of sperm), so the verbs must be in plural form: 'bante hain' and 'karte hain', not the singular 'banta hain' and 'karta hain'.

original_english: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number to half so that gametes have 23 chromosomes.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis chromosome number ko aadha kar deta hai isliye gametes mein 23 chromosomes ka hota hai.
hinglish_with_error: Meiosis chromosome number ko aadha kar deta hai isliye gametes mein 23 chromosomes ka hota hai.
error_type: incorrect postposition + wrong plural verb form
error_explanation: The postposition 'ka' is incorrectly used with 'chromosomes'. The correct construction is simply 'chromosomes hote hain' (chromosomes are present), without 'ka'.

original_english: Vegetatively propagated plants are genetically identical because they come from a single parent.
hinglish_roman: Vegetatively propagate hue plants genetically identical hote hain kyunki woh ek hi parent ka se aate hain.
hinglish_with_error: Vegetatively propagate hue plants genetically identical hote hain kyunki woh ek hi parent ka se aate hain.
error_explanation: 'Ka se' is redundant; either 'ka' (of/belonging to) or 'se' (from) should be used, not both. The correct form is 'ek hi parent se aate hain' meaning 'come from a single parent'.

original_english: The Earth is home to an enormous variety of life forms, and this immense variety of living organisms is known as biodiversity.
hinglish_roman: Prithvi par bahut saari life forms payi jaati hain, aur is vishal variety of living organisms ko biodiversity kehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Biodiversity is essential for us and every organism plays a role in keeping nature stable and functioning.
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity hamare liye essential hai aur har organism nature ko stable aur functional rakhne mein ek role play karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Microscopic algae in the oceans release most of the oxygen we breathe.
hinglish_roman: Oceans mein microscopic algae zyaadatar oxygen release karti hain jo hum saans lete hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fungi and bacteria decompose fallen leaves and convert waste into manure, making the soil fertile.
hinglish_roman: Fungi aur bacteria gire hue patte decompose karte hain aur waste ko manure mein convert karte hain, jisse mitti fertile banti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Birds, bees and bats pollinate flowers, while plants capture sunlight to prepare food that supports nearly all life on the planet.
hinglish_roman: Pakshi, bees aur bats phoolon ko pollinate karte hain, jabki plants sunlight capture karke almost sabhi jeevon ka food prepare karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: India's natural landscape is diverse, with mountains in the north, deserts in the west, and rainforests in the North East.
hinglish_roman: India ka natural landscape bahut diverse hai - uttar mein mountains, paschim mein desert, aur North East mein rainforests hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Species restricted to particular regions of the world and not found naturally anywhere else are called endemic species.
hinglish_roman: Jo species sirf kisi ek particular region mein payi jaati hain aur kahin aur naturally nahi milti, unhe endemic species kehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Nilgiri tahr, Lion-tailed macaque, Nepenthes khasiana and Neelakurinji are endemic species found only in India.
hinglish_roman: Nilgiri tahr, Lion-tailed macaque, Nepenthes khasiana aur Neelakurinji sirf India mein payi jaane waali endemic species hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Regions that support a large number of endemic species and have undergone significant habitat loss are known as biodiversity hotspots.
hinglish_roman: Jo regions bahut saari endemic species ko support karte hain aur jahaan significant habitat loss hua ho, unhe biodiversity hotspots kehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The Western Ghats, Indo-Burma including North East India, the Himalayas, and Sundaland are some examples of global biodiversity hotspots.
hinglish_roman: Western Ghats, Indo-Burma jisme North East India bhi shaamil hai, Himalayas aur Sundaland kuch global biodiversity hotspots ke examples hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Small differences among individuals affected their chances of survival and reproduction, helping them adapt to changed conditions.
hinglish_roman: Individuals mein choti choti differences unke survival aur reproduction ke chances ko affect karti thi, jinse woh changed conditions mein adapt kar sake.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Scientists group and classify organisms based on their shared characteristics and evolutionary relationships.
hinglish_roman: Scientists organisms ko unke shared characteristics aur evolutionary relationships ke aadhar par group aur classify karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: External features like shape, size and body organisation are used as one of the criteria to classify living organisms.
hinglish_roman: Shape, size aur body organisation jaise external features living organisms ko classify karne ke ek criterion ke roop mein use kiye jaate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Mode of nutrition, whether autotrophic or heterotrophic, is another important criterion for classifying organisms.
hinglish_roman: Nutrition ka mode, yaani autotrophic hai ya heterotrophic, organisms ko classify karne ka ek aur important criterion hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Cell structure, whether the organism is unicellular or multicellular, eukaryote or prokaryote, is a key classification criterion.
hinglish_roman: Cell structure - organism unicellular hai ya multicellular, eukaryote hai ya prokaryote - classification ka ek key criterion hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Genetic similarity, studied through DNA analysis, helps scientists understand shared ancestry among organisms.
hinglish_roman: Genetic similarity, jo DNA analysis se study ki jaati hai, scientists ko organisms ke beech shared ancestry samajhne mein help karti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Similar features in organisms suggest that they have evolved from common ancestors.
hinglish_roman: Organisms mein similar features yeh suggest karte hain ki woh common ancestors se evolved hue hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Just like organising a library makes finding books easier, classifying organisms helps us study millions of life forms systematically.
hinglish_roman: Jaise library mein books ko organize karne se unhe dhoondna aasaan hota hai, waisi hi organisms ko classify karne se laakhon life forms ka systematic study ho sakta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Biological classification is a scientific system of grouping living organisms based on their similarities and differences.
hinglish_roman: Biological classification ek scientific system hai jisme living organisms ko unki similarities aur differences ke aadhar par group kiya jaata hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Classification supports biodiversity conservation by identifying organisms that are under the threat of extinction.
hinglish_roman: Classification un organisms ki pehchaan karke biodiversity conservation mein madad karta hai jo extinction ke khatre mein hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Aristotle grouped animals based on their habitat — land, water and air — in the 4th century BCE.
hinglish_roman: Aristotle ne 4th century BCE mein animals ko unke habitat ke aadhar par — zameen, paani aur hawa — group kiya tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: In the two kingdom system introduced in the 18th century, all living organisms were divided into Plantae and Animalia.
hinglish_roman: 18th century mein introduce kiya gaya two kingdom system mein sabhi living organisms ko Plantae aur Animalia mein divide kiya gaya tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The two kingdom system created confusion because organisms like Amoeba and Paramecium are unicellular and could not be clearly placed in Plantae or Animalia.
hinglish_roman: Two kingdom system mein confusion tha kyunki Amoeba aur Paramecium jaise organisms unicellular hain aur inhe clearly Plantae ya Animalia mein nahi rakha ja sakta tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Ernst Haeckel added a third kingdom Protista in 1866 to include unicellular microscopic organisms.
hinglish_roman: Ernst Haeckel ne 1866 mein unicellular microscopic organisms ko include karne ke liye teesra kingdom Protista add kiya.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Since bacteria lack a membrane-bound nucleus unlike Amoeba, they were placed in a separate kingdom called Monera, leading to a four kingdom system.
hinglish_roman: Kyunki bacteria mein Amoeba ke unlike membrane-bound nucleus nahi hota, isliye bacteria ko alag kingdom Monera mein rakha gaya, jisse four kingdom system bana.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Robert H. Whittaker proposed the five kingdom classification in 1969, which includes Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.
hinglish_roman: Robert H. Whittaker ne 1969 mein five kingdom classification propose kiya, jisme Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae aur Animalia shamil hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: In the five kingdom classification, organisms are grouped based on cell type, cell structure, level of organisation and mode of nutrition.
hinglish_roman: Five kingdom classification mein organisms ko cell type, cell structure, level of organisation aur mode of nutrition ke basis par group kiya jaata hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Monera includes unicellular prokaryotes such as bacteria, archaea and cyanobacteria.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Monera mein unicellular prokaryotes aate hain jaise bacteria, archaea aur cyanobacteria.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Bacteria are found everywhere, including soil, water, air, hot springs and even inside the human body.
hinglish_roman: Bacteria har jagah paaye jaate hain — mitti, paani, hawa, hot springs aur yahan tak ki human body ke andar bhi.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Cyanobacteria were among the first organisms to produce oxygen through photosynthesis, about 2.5 billion years ago.
hinglish_roman: Cyanobacteria un pehle organisms mein se the jo approximately 2.5 billion saal pehle photosynthesis ke zariye oxygen produce karte the.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Protista includes all single-celled eukaryotes such as Amoeba, Paramecium and Euglena.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Protista mein sabhi single-celled eukaryotes aate hain jaise Amoeba, Paramecium aur Euglena.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Protists are an important link in aquatic food chains — some produce oxygen while others serve as food for small animals.
hinglish_roman: Protists aquatic food chains mein ek important link hain — kuch oxygen produce karte hain jabki doosre chote animals ke liye food ka kaam karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Fungi are mostly multicellular eukaryotes with cell walls made of chitin.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Fungi mein zyaadatar multicellular eukaryotes hote hain jinki cell wall chitin se bani hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fungi are important decomposers that feed on dead organic matter such as fallen leaves, twigs or dead organisms.
hinglish_roman: Fungi important decomposers hote hain jo dead organic matter jaise gire patte, twigsaur marey hue organisms par feed karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Yeast is a unicellular fungus and since its cell wall is made of chitin, it is placed under Kingdom Fungi.
hinglish_roman: Yeast ek unicellular fungus hai aur kyunki iski cell wall chitin se bani hai, ise Kingdom Fungi mein rakha gaya hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fungi like Aspergillus and Penicillium are used to make enzymes and antibiotics.
hinglish_roman: Aspergillus aur Penicillium jaise fungi enzymes aur antibiotics banane ke kaam aate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Plantae includes multicellular autotrophic organisms whose cells have a rigid cell wall primarily made of cellulose.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Plantae mein multicellular autotrophic organisms aate hain jinke cells mein ek rigid cell wall hoti hai jo mainly cellulose se bani hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Thallophytes are among the simplest plant forms, mostly found in water or moist environments, and form a simple undifferentiated body called a thallus.
hinglish_roman: Thallophytes sabse simple plant forms mein se hain, jo zyaadatar paani ya nami waale environments mein paaye jaate hain aur ek simple undifferentiated body banate hain jise thallus kehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Bryophytes like mosses and liverworts represent an important shift from water to land but still require moisture for survival.
hinglish_roman: Bryophytes jaise mosses aur liverworts paani se zameen par aane ka ek important shift represent karte hain lekin inhe abhi bhi nami ki zaroorat hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because they require water for reproduction.
hinglish_roman: Bryophytes ko plant kingdom ke amphibians kaha jaata hai kyunki inhe reproduction ke liye paani ki zaroorat padti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Pteridophytes like ferns possess true roots, stems and leaves, along with vascular tissues — xylem and phloem — for transporting water and food.
hinglish_roman: Ferns jaise pteridophytes mein true roots, stems aur leaves hote hain, saath hi xylem aur phloem jaise vascular tissues bhi hote hain jo paani aur food transport karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Pteridophytes still depend on water for reproduction and do not produce seeds.
hinglish_roman: Pteridophytes abhi bhi reproduction ke liye paani par depend karte hain aur seeds produce nahi karte.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Gymnosperms like pines and cycads are well adapted to cold and dry regions; their needle-like leaves reduce water loss.
hinglish_roman: Pines aur cycads jaise gymnosperms thande aur sukhe regions ke liye achhi tarah se adapt hain; unke needle-like patte paani ka nuksan kam karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Gymnosperms do not require water for fertilisation; their seeds are not enclosed in fruits but are exposed on cones.
hinglish_roman: Gymnosperms ko fertilisation ke liye paani ki zaroorat nahi hoti; unke seeds fruits mein band nahi hote balki cones par khule hote hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Angiosperms or flowering plants represent the most complex plant body organisation and are the most diverse plant group on Earth.
hinglish_roman: Angiosperms yaani flowering plants sabse complex plant body organisation represent karte hain aur yeh Earth par sabse zyaada diverse plant group hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Angiosperms produce flowers and fruits — flowers attract pollinators and fruits help disperse seeds to new locations.
hinglish_roman: Angiosperms phool aur fruits produce karte hain — phool pollinators ko attract karte hain aur fruits seeds ko nayi jagahon tak pahunchane mein madad karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Animalia includes multicellular heterotrophic organisms that depend on other organisms for food.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Animalia mein multicellular heterotrophic organisms aate hain jo apne food ke liye doosre organisms par depend karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Animals are classified into non-chordata and chordata based on the presence or absence of a notochord.
hinglish_roman: Animals ko notochord ki presence ya absence ke aadhar par non-chordata aur chordata mein classify kiya jaata hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Porifera or sponges are multicellular animals that lack true tissues and organs, with numerous pores allowing water to flow through their bodies.
hinglish_roman: Porifera yaani sponges multicellular animals hain jinmein true tissues aur organs nahi hote, aur unke body mein bahut saare pores hote hain jisse paani andar-bahar bahta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Cnidarians like Hydra, jellyfish and corals have tissue-level organisation and use tentacles for capturing prey.
hinglish_roman: Hydra, jellyfish aur corals jaise cnidarians mein tissue-level organisation hota hai aur yeh shikaar pakadne ke liye tentacles use karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Platyhelminthes or flatworms show bilateral symmetry, which allows better coordination of movement and directional activity.
hinglish_roman: Platyhelminthes yaani flatworms mein bilateral symmetry hoti hai, jisse movement ka better coordination aur directional activity possible hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Nematoda or roundworms have an elongated cylindrical body with two openings — a mouth and an anus.
hinglish_roman: Nematoda yaani roundworms ka body elongated aur cylindrical hota hai jisme do openings hote hain — ek mouth aur ek anus.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Annelids like earthworms have segmented bodies, which allows greater flexibility and more precise control of movement.
hinglish_roman: Earthworms jaise annelids ka body segmented hota hai, jisse movement mein zyaada flexibility aur precise control milta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Arthropods have a hard external skeleton called an exoskeleton that provides protection and reduces water loss.
hinglish_roman: Arthropods mein ek hard external skeleton hota hai jise exoskeleton kehte hain, jo protection deta hai aur paani ka loss kam karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Mollusca like snails, squids and octopuses have soft bodies, with many having a shell for protection.
hinglish_roman: Snails, squids aur octopuses jaise mollusca ka body soft hota hai aur bahut se molluscs ke paas protection ke liye ek shell hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Echinoderms like starfish and sea urchins possess a hard internal skeleton made of calcium carbonate.
hinglish_roman: Starfish aur sea urchins jaise echinoderms mein calcium carbonate se bana ek hard internal skeleton hota hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Protochordates like Amphioxus possess a notochord at least once during their life and help us understand how chordates evolved from simpler forms.
hinglish_roman: Amphioxus jaise protochordates mein apni zindagi mein kam se kam ek baar notochord zaroor hoti hai, aur yeh samajhne mein help karte hain ki chordates kaise simpler forms se evolve hue.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Vertebrates possess a vertebral column or backbone that supports the body and protects vital organs like the brain and spinal cord.
hinglish_roman: Vertebrates mein ek vertebral column yaani backbone hota hai jo body ko support karta hai aur brain aur spinal cord jaise vital organs ki raksha karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Vertebrates are classified into five groups — fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals — based on habitat, body covering and reproduction.
hinglish_roman: Vertebrates ko paanch groups mein classify kiya jaata hai — fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds aur mammals — habitat, body covering aur reproduction ke basis par.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fish have fins and gills that allow them to move and breathe in water.
hinglish_roman: Fish ke paas fins aur gills hote hain jo unhe paani mein chalne aur saans lene mein help karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Birds have feathers and hollow bones, which make flight possible.
hinglish_roman: Pakshiyon ke paas feathers aur hollow bones hote hain jo udon ko possible banate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Mammals have mammary glands that produce milk for their young, improving the survival of offspring.
hinglish_roman: Mammals mein mammary glands hote hain jo apne bachhon ke liye milk produce karte hain, jisse unke survival chances badh jaate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Classification follows a hierarchical arrangement from Kingdom at the broadest level down to Species at the most specific level.
hinglish_roman: Classification ek hierarchical arrangement follow karta hai — sabse broad level Kingdom se lekar sabse specific level Species tak.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The levels of classification in order from broadest to most specific are: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus and Species.
hinglish_roman: Classification ke levels broad se specific order mein hain: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus aur Species.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: At each lower level of the hierarchy, organisms share more common features with each other.
hinglish_roman: Hierarchy ke har neeche waale level par organisms ke beech zyaada common features hote hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The tiger belongs to Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Carnivora, Family Felidae, Genus Panthera and Species P. tigris.
hinglish_roman: Tiger Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Carnivora, Family Felidae, Genus Panthera aur Species P. tigris se belong karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Binomial nomenclature is a universal system of naming living organisms, where every organism is given a two-part scientific name.
hinglish_roman: Binomial nomenclature living organisms ko naam dene ka ek universal system hai jisme har organism ko ek do-hissa scientific naam diya jaata hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Binomial nomenclature was introduced by Carolus Linnaeus in the 18th century.
hinglish_roman: Binomial nomenclature ko 18th century mein Carolus Linnaeus ne introduce kiya tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: In the binomial system, the scientific name has two parts — the genus name comes first with a capital letter, followed by the species name in lowercase.
hinglish_roman: Binomial system mein scientific naam ke do hisse hote hain — pehle genus naam capital letter se, phir species naam lowercase mein likhte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The scientific name Panthera tigris is written in italics when printed, with Panthera being the genus and tigris the species.
hinglish_roman: Panthera tigris ka scientific naam print mein italics mein likha jaata hai, jisme Panthera genus hai aur tigris species.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: A genus groups closely related species; for example, Panthera tigris (tiger) and Panthera leo (lion) are both in the genus Panthera.
hinglish_roman: Ek genus closely related species ko group karta hai; jaise Panthera tigris yaani tiger aur Panthera leo yaani lion dono Panthera genus mein hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Carl Woese proposed the three domain system in 1977, dividing life into Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya based on genetic data.
hinglish_roman: Carl Woese ne 1977 mein teen domain system propose kiya jisme genetic data ke aadhar par life ko Bacteria, Archaea aur Eukarya mein divide kiya gaya.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fossils are preserved remains of plants and animals found in layers of rocks, sand and mud, providing evidence of how life has changed over millions of years.
hinglish_roman: Fossils pedh-paudhon aur jaanwaron ke preserved remains hote hain jo rocks, ret aur mitti ki perton mein milte hain, aur yeh laakhon saalon mein jeevan kaise badla iski evidence dete hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Human activities like pollution, deforestation, overuse of resources and climate change are reducing biodiversity.
hinglish_roman: Pradushan, deforestation, resources ka zyaada use aur climate change jaise human activities biodiversity ko kam kar rahi hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: When one species disappears, others that depend on it may also decline, highlighting the interconnected nature of ecosystems.
hinglish_roman: Jab ek species khatam ho jaati hai, to usse dependent doosri species bhi ghatti ja sakti hain, jo ecosystems ki interconnected nature ko highlight karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Can you explain what biodiversity means and why it is important for us?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap explain kar sakte hain biodiversity ka matlab kya hai aur yeh hamare liye kyun important hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the definition of endemic species? Can you give me an example from India?
hinglish_roman: Endemic species ki definition kya hoti hai? Kya aap mujhe India se koi example de sakte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition?
hinglish_roman: Autotrophic aur heterotrophic nutrition mein kya difference hota hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Can you explain what binomial nomenclature is and why scientists use it?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap explain kar sakte hain binomial nomenclature kya hota hai aur scientists ise kyun use karte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between bryophytes and pteridophytes?
hinglish_roman: Bryophytes aur pteridophytes mein kya antar hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Can you explain Whittaker's five kingdom classification with the criteria used?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap Whittaker ka five kingdom classification aur usme use kiye gaye criteria explain kar sakte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What are biodiversity hotspots? Why is the Western Ghats considered one?
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity hotspots kya hote hain? Western Ghats ko ek hotspot kyun maana jaata hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the main difference between invertebrates and vertebrates?
hinglish_roman: Invertebrates aur vertebrates mein main difference kya hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Can you explain what a notochord is and what role it plays in animal classification?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap explain kar sakte hain notochord kya hota hai aur animal classification mein iska kya role hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is Kingdom Monera? Which organisms are placed in it and why?
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Monera kya hai? Ismein kaun se organisms rakhe jaate hain aur kyun?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between gymnosperms and angiosperms? Can you give examples of each?
hinglish_roman: Gymnosperms aur angiosperms mein kya antar hai? Kya aap dono ke examples de sakte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: How does hierarchical classification work? What does each level represent?
hinglish_roman: Hierarchical classification kaise kaam karta hai? Har level kya represent karta hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Why are fungi classified in a separate kingdom even though they look like plants?
hinglish_roman: Fungi ko ek alag kingdom mein kyun classify kiya jaata hai jabki woh plants ki tarah dikhte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the definition of a species in biological classification?
hinglish_roman: Biological classification mein species ki definition kya hoti hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells? Can you give examples of organisms in each?
hinglish_roman: Prokaryotic aur eukaryotic cells mein kya antar hai? Kya dono ke organisms ke examples de sakte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Biodiversity is essential for every living organism on Earth.
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity har ek living organism ke liye Earth par jaruri hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Biodiversity har ek living organism ke liye Earth pe jaruri hota hai.
gec_explanation: 'Biodiversity' is singular and feminine in context; 'hota' (masculine agreement) should be 'hoti' or simply 'hai' for gender-neutral agreement.

original_english: Fungi are classified in a separate kingdom because they obtain nutrients by absorption from dead matter.
hinglish_roman: Fungi ko alag kingdom mein classify kiya gaya hai kyunki woh dead matter se absorption ke zariye nutrients prapt karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Fungi ko alag kingdom mein classify kiya gaya hai kyunki woh dead matter se absorb karke nutrients prapt karta hain.
gec_explanation: 'Fungi' is plural in usage here; the verb should be 'karte hain' not 'karta hain'.

original_english: Pteridophytes have vascular tissues — xylem and phloem — for transporting water and food throughout the plant.
hinglish_roman: Pteridophytes mein vascular tissues hote hain — xylem aur phloem — jo poore plant mein paani aur food transport karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Pteridophytes mein vascular tissue hote hain — xylem aur phloem — jo poore plant mein paani aur food transport karta hain.
gec_explanation: The subject 'xylem aur phloem' is plural; the correct verb form is 'karte hain', not 'karta hain'.

original_english: Binomial nomenclature was introduced by Carolus Linnaeus so that scientists worldwide could use a common naming system.
hinglish_roman: Binomial nomenclature Carolus Linnaeus ne isliye introduce kiya taaki duniyabhar ke scientists ek common naming system use kar sakein.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Binomial nomenclature Carolus Linnaeus ne isliye introduce kiya tha taaki duniyabhar ke scientists ek common naming system use kar saka.
gec_explanation: After 'taaki' (so that), the subjunctive form 'sakein' (plural) is correct, not 'saka' (singular past masculine).

original_english: When one species becomes extinct, the other species that depend on it may also be affected.
hinglish_roman: Jab ek species extinct ho jaati hai, to usse dependent doosri species bhi prabhavit ho sakti hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Jab ek species extinct ho jaata hai, to usse dependent doosri species bhi prabhavit ho sakti hain.
gec_explanation: 'Species' is treated as feminine in Hindi; 'ho jaata' (masculine) should be 'ho jaati' (feminine).
